summary: Step 13 verification of the 3 new features + demo seed. Created /app/backend/tests/test_step13.py (20 pytest cases, 17 PASS / 3 intentional defect-documenting FAILs, ~8s, no AI needed) and ran 3 Playwright passes against the public URL. VERIFIED WORKING: (A) Resident Chat Thread — POST /api/residents/thread returns issue + 8 chronologically-sorted interactions for Nathan Brooks/603, 404 for wrong resident and for unknown issue_id; resident portal My Requests shows 1 card with 'Reopened' badge + reopened banner, toggle-thread-{id} flips label View/Hide conversation and renders thread-{id} with 8 bubbles, resident msgs right-aligned (justify-end, dark), system/staff/ai left-aligned with distinct colours, hides again on second click, 0 error nodes. (B) Trend Insights — GET /api/insights returns total_repeat=3, by_category [complaint 1, noise 1, maintenance 1], by_unit [451,412,603], weekly [2026-W34:1, 2026-W35:2]; sums match total; 401 without auth; nav-insights routes to /staff/insights and insight-total/insight-categories/insight-units/insight-weekly all render with real bars. (C) Answer Approval — POST /api/issues/{id}/approve-answer posts the answer as an 'ai' interaction + a system 'Suggested answer approved and sent by ...' note, sets lane=RESOLVE/status=resolved/resolved_at/auto_response, clears suggested_response, no _id leak; persisted on GET /api/issues/{id}; empty/whitespace answer -> 400, unknown id -> 404, unauthenticated -> 401. UI: suggested-response card pre-fills approve-answer-input, edited text is accepted, approve-answer-btn shows 'Answer approved and sent to the resident.' toast and the sheet re-renders as Resolved with the edited answer in AUTO-RESOLVED FROM DOCUMENTS. SEED: /api/dashboard = total 20, handled 5, actions 5, reviews 10, failed 3, confirmed 100%, median 120s; 20 issues across RESOLVE/ACTION/REVIEW with populated AI fields + human_attention_score; Unit 603 = reopened/REVIEW/attempts 1/failed_resolution true/score 96/6-field review_summary/repeat_complaint; Unit 412 = REVIEW noise, contact_count 3, review brief; /api/incidents/detect returns exactly one incident, 4 residents, units 701-704. REGRESSION: dashboard tab filters via testids REVIEW 10 / ACTION 5 / AI Resolved 5 / Failed Resolutions 3 / All Issues 20, search '603' -> 1 row, score column intact, unit-603 sheet renders review-outcome + failed-resolution-banner + repeat-complaint-banner + attention-score, shared-incident banner correct, Property Knowledge lists 4 ready docs. DB restored to exactly 20 issues / 45 interactions / 4 docs, 0 TEST leftovers.

critical.issue: No guard on lane / suggested_response. Reproduced: cloned an open ACTION maintenance ticket (no suggested_response) and POSTed {answer:'probe'} -> 200 with lane=RESOLVE, status=resolved, assigned_team=null. Staff (or any bug/mis-click) can close an open work order with an arbitrary 'approved answer'. Should 400 unless issue.lane=='REVIEW' and issue.suggested_response is set. Same class as the iteration_6 HIGH defect. Test: test_step13.py::test_approve_answer_rejects_non_review_issue

DEMO GAP: not a single seeded issue has suggested_response (all 20 have suggested_response=null), so the Answer Approval feature (approve-answer-input / approve-answer-btn card) NEVER renders anywhere in the seeded demo — the feature is undemoable without hand-editing the DB (I had to clone an issue in Mongo to exercise it). Seed at least one REVIEW issue (e.g. the Unit 337 parking policy-conflict or a FAQ-style question) with a suggested_response. Test: test_step13.py::test_seed_has_review_issue_with_suggested_response

minor.issue: Thread order is illogical: interactions come back as [resident report, system ack, staff 'Plumber replaced the drain seal', resident '✓ Confirmed resolved', ai 'Is everything working now? Please confirm', system 'Marked complete — awaiting resident confirmation', resident 'leaking again', system 'Previous resolution failed']. The resident's confirmation (idx 3) is timestamped BEFORE the confirmation prompt (idx 4) and before 'Marked complete' (idx 5), so in the resident chat the confirmation appears to answer a question that has not been asked yet. Expected per the storyline: repair -> marked complete -> confirmation prompt -> resident confirmed. Test: test_step13.py::test_unit603_thread_chronology_is_logical

Cluster keyword is unstable/generic for the water outage: two identical calls returned keyword 'water' and then keyword 'coming' for the same 701-704 cluster (tie-break on token counts, 'coming' from "no water coming out of any tap"). resident_count/units are correct, but any UI that surfaces the keyword can show 'coming'. Carries over the iteration_6 recommendation to score keywords from entities / domain nouns.

After approving an answer on the Unit 337 policy-conflict issue, the issue is RESOLVE/resolved but policy_conflict stays true and human_attention_score stays 60, so the detail sheet still shows the red 'REVIEW — POLICY CONFLICT' banner and HUMAN ATTENTION SCORE 60 next to the resolved answer. finalize_attention() should zero/降 the score for resolved issues and the conflict banner should be suppressed once resolved.

design_issues.screen: Staff issue detail Sheet (after Approve & Send)
issues: Resolved issue still displays 'REVIEW — POLICY CONFLICT' banner and attention score 60 alongside the approved answer — contradictory state.
Confirmation bubble '✓ Confirmed resolved' renders above the 'Is everything working now?' prompt (seed timestamp ordering) — reads backwards in the demo.
Stat-card label 'Failed Resolutions' duplicates the filter-tab label; text-based selection/clicking is ambiguous (testids exist, so tests are fine, but consider distinct wording).

action_items: HIGH: guard approve-answer — 400 unless lane=='REVIEW' and suggested_response is present; do not clear assigned_team on ACTION tickets.
HIGH: seed at least one REVIEW issue with a suggested_response so the Answer Approval feature is visible in the demo (currently 0/20).
MEDIUM: fix Unit 603 seed interaction timestamps so the confirmation prompt + 'marked complete' precede the resident's '✓ Confirmed resolved' reply.
LOW: suppress policy-conflict/review banners and lower human_attention_score once an issue is resolved via approve-answer.
LOW: stabilise incident keyword selection (entities/domain nouns) — 'coming' vs 'water' for the 701-704 cluster.
critical_code_review_comments: approve_answer() (server.py:1276) trusts any issue id and any answer string; add lane/suggested_response validation and keep assigned_team when the underlying work order is still open.

GET /api/insights loads every issue into Python (find({}).to_list(5000)) and Counters in-process; move to a $match/$group aggregation and cap the response, otherwise it degrades linearly with issue volume.

/api/residents/thread does resident lookup by (name, unit) plaintext — any resident's full conversation is readable by anyone who knows a neighbour's name+unit. Acceptable for a demo, but flag as a privacy TODO (token/magic-link per request).

server.py is now 1483 lines (triage, auth, documents, dashboard, incidents, insights, thread, approvals) — split into routers/services; both new endpoints were appended below the document handlers, so route grouping is already inconsistent.

Insights 'weekly' buckets use the issue created_at, not the repeat/failure date, so a repeat detected this week still lands in the week the issue was first opened — the 'week over week' framing in the UI copy is misleading.

rca_of_the_issue: approve_answer() in server.py only checks existence of the issue and non-empty answer, then unconditionally writes lane=RESOLVE/status=resolved/assigned_team=None — so it doubles as an 'unconditional close' endpoint for ACTION tickets. Separately, seed_demo.py builds REVIEW issues with review_summary but never sets suggested_response, and IssueDetailSheet only renders the approval card when issue.suggested_response is truthy (line 284), which is why the feature is invisible on seeded data. The Unit 603 chronology issue is purely seed-side: the interaction created_at offsets place the resident confirmation earlier than the ai prompt/system completion notes, and both API and UI sort strictly by created_at.
